correctness.rationale: A full directed circuit cannot pass through a guru, and on the interior of an arc the only directed cycle possible is an adjacent clockwise/counterclockwise two-cycle. Excluding that pair forces a prefix pointing to the first endpoint followed by a suffix pointing to the second; every cut is feasible and the uniform law makes distinct cuts independent. The weight vector is the deterministic term plus the sum of each cut variable times e_i−e_{i+1}. The discrete uniform variance m(m+2)/12 gives the stated Laplacian, with two separate contributions for parallel arcs at k=2. Same-ballot arcs have constant contribution with multiplicity and opposite-ballot arcs give one copy of every intervening tally; coefficient sums give exactly the two thresholds. The convolution bound counts arithmetic operations, not bit operations. In the two-guru case the central sum on an even cycle is attained once for every value of the shorter cut variable, so the tie probability is the reciprocal of one plus the longer arc interior length. Its equality cases and the symmetry of the win probabilities follow, including zero-length interiors. A separate bounded enumeration found no mismatch for all 218 root sets on n=3,…,7 and all 3,212 associated ballot patterns; the proof does not depend on that finite check.
residual_risks: Only fixed gurus, labeled simple cycles and a uniform law conditioned on feasibility. The extrema assume opposing ballots and even n; odd n precludes ties, not necessarily equal tie-inclusive counts in unrelated models.

originality.rationale: The unmarked count and the underlying rooted-forest structure are standard; the supported distinct claim is the explicit joint component-size and tally laws for this conditional election model and the sharp opposing-guru positional tie consequence. Neither the inspected general decision/branching work nor the closest cycle record supplies these marked formulas under the stated sampling law. The elementary uniform-sum calculation alone is not claimed as original.
residual_risks: Best-of-knowledge only. Full primary text of 1b77836d9c13 was not accessible in the mirror; its indexed model differs, but exact coverage by that text is not ruled out. General rooted-forest machinery and independent gap deletions are credited, not claimed new.

value.rationale: The exact winner count is a tractable, natural special case of a proposed counting problem and the joint law also supplies coalition uncertainty without re-enumerating orientations. Most notably, with two opposing gurus both candidates have the same strict-win chance, yet guru locations change the tie probability by nearly a factor of two. That sharp dependence is a useful benchmark for delegation models beyond just counting forests.
residual_risks: The method exploits cycle separability; it does not settle the general counting problem or support claims about empirical voters.
